Changes at 40a3b4b:
Resolved all suggested changes above.

Update a07b0c5:
1. Resolve unit test errors.
2. Make thumbnail created on import (`EditorInterface::make_scene_preview`) uses the same math as `EditorPackedScenePreviewPlugin::_construct_scene_3d`, so thumbnails look identical no matter the creation method.
3. Set `docks/filesystem/thumbnail_file_size_threshold` min value to 0 so we can actually disable background preview creation.

Update cfa8636f350b16efa7609504c4ec2aea3b82df19 :
1. Rebased to master 7ed0b6167618f9c8c5df87c7e83da6003c081368
2. Make `*.scn` files always be ignored by scene thumbnail generator, as I don't know how to read it without calling `ResourceLoader::load()`

---

Removed tasks from TODO:
> In thumbnail metadata, mark large scenes that are not handled by preview generator

> When docks/filesystem/thumbnail_file_size_threshold is changed, queue all scene files that were ignored (uses the implemented metadata)

As it complicates the code base and requires a lot of workaround just for this specific feature. Because the current code base uses a lot of callbacks & notifications to manage states and queue thumbnails. I personally think `editor/editor_node.cpp` should be refactored to favor direct function calls and coupling, to make implementing core features more easily, for now it handles everything like plugins, and it's difficult to resolve race conditions when multiple features are working together on the same file (scene file, specifically)
> Minimize and clean up redundant comments in this PR

Is not important, and there isn't much redundant comments anyway.
Should put more work on testing now.

Update e9e2e54:

rebased to master dec5a373d97cbadce5e1fabe6095ae9957ff3aa6, resolved conflicts.

> multi-threaded scene loading still isn't possible now

There is `ResourceLoader::load_threaded_request()`. It might still cause stutters, but they are rare and very minor (although I never tried it with 3D scenes).

As a GODOT user for many years, I can say from the bottom of my heart that I am in love with GODOT and all its wonderful features, and that I am in love with this loving and cooperative community. Therefore, I am not surprised why we are climbing to the top so quickly. ❤️
Any chance of this getting merged for 4.7?

> Make EditorPackedScenePreviewPlugin::_create_node_lookup_table return a pointer HashMap<String, int> * instead of a copy:

Why not a reference?
Don't use `new` with a HashMap.

Something is wrong with preview cache. Seems like old-style previews are still being generated and they will get used if you save the scene without any changes:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29a84a2a-a2db-4518-8b1c-865e16d00d56

The new previews only generate if the scene was modified.

> Something is wrong with preview cache. Seems like old-style previews are still being generated and they will get used if you save the scene without any changes

@KoBeWi 

One thing to note is as the plugin nature of preview generator, I found it relatively hard to talk upwards to work with the fallback old-style thumbnail creation code. And will make the thumbnail creation process stateful while users are doing other things. The thumbnail queuing system is in-place so I want to expand from there.

So the next best thing I could do is actually, **the fall-backs are executed first**. It's like this:

fallback thumbnailer captured and save the image (in `EditorNode::_save_scene_with_preview`) -> queues plugin thumbnail creation -> this PR generates thumbnail.

So whenever we abort thumbnail creation in the plugin, it "fall-backs" to the old style because it's already present and not overwritten. I think the issue you mentioned can be solved by checking file hash at fallback thumbnailer, working on that.

> When determining if a scene is 2D or 3D, we don't count nodes under a Viewport derived node.

Yeah sorry, in my scene the 3D node wasn't inside viewport.

> no 2D scenes will need a single 3D node in it (IMO, correct me if wrong)

You can have 2D scene with 3D nodes used as background. I have one such scene in my project, but yeah, this is a very rare case. Probably not worth considering.

I'm not sure if this complexity is worth it. In most cases checking only one level of dependencies should be enough. There is also a risk that scanning file sizes can become more expensive than generating the preview.

Also why a HashMap? You could either return the summed size of dependencies (there is no reason to collect the sizes and then sum them later), or use a HashSet (to avoid duplicates) and then read file sizes after collecting all paths.

@KoBeWi 

> I'm not sure if this complexity is worth it. In most cases checking only one level of dependencies should be enough. There is also a risk that scanning file sizes can become more expensive than generating the preview.

Scanning file sizes operates on a thread, once the check passes, generating the preview will have processes that can only be done in main thread. User will mostly experience lag on creating preview scenes, not while scanning files. (There's a lot of *unless...* here but in those cases their system is already unresponsive)

I assume your concern is there will be a scene that has few hundred dependencies that slows down the thumbnailer because we need to lookup all those files. But with the queue system, there will be no duplicated requests, and only processes one resource at a time, so the performance cost is constant, it just takes longer.

Also In contrast, a scene so complex that took 1 minute to load and instantiate, might just need few seconds to check all its dependencies' sizes. That's probably the maximum sized scene people will build with this engine realistically.

In the end, the use case that will benefit from this PR most are scenes that acted as prefabs, which generally is small in size. Generating thumbnails for level scenes is second priority and should be careful, we can silently set a hard-cap of "if scene has over 200 dependencies, quit scanning files, assume it's large, abort and fallback" just in case, the last thing I want is people having large scenes in their projects and complains about this PR giving them lags, and we need to address it in a short time, which is stressful.

> HashSet (to avoid duplicates) and then read file sizes after collecting all paths.

Good idea I'll try this instead.

(*deleted outdated code*)

I am not sure if we should expose a editor setting `thumbnail_res_count_threshold` in this case, as user might not find it useful.
I can finally see my modular models imported using a `EditorScenePostImport` 🎉

Allow me to make a suggestion. When we say small, large, or normal, these are relative things that differ from one person to another. There may be games that contain complex scenes with small scale objects, and there may be games that target an audience with powerful devices. Forcing a specific size or count on them would not be suitable. Therefore, I suggest making it an option in Project Settings, with a default value that you agree upon. Thank you!
I wish we could preserve the rounded corners in the previews. The difference is visible in the video in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112060#issuecomment-4229457535

> Therefore, I suggest making it an option in Project Settings, with a default value that you agree upon. Thank you!

Project settings shouldn't include editor-related things. If anything, it should be an editor setting (they can be overridden per project).

I am testing this PR by using the artifact build for windows. ## On my current project (John Space) I can say that after a few minutes, Godot became irresponsive for several minutes, still waiting. Here are the errors I succeeded to take screenshots of (not all seems related to the changes from this PR): The task manager tells that Godot is using ~16% of CPU and 1.6GO of memory at the moment. I will edit this post if I get more details. EDIT: After several minutes waiting, I decided to close Godot. ## On my Open Source Starter Kit On that project things went smoothly, and all the thumbnail loaded successful I think! Note that you can try it for yourself using the [project here](https://github.com/Nodragem/top-down-action-adventure-starter-kit). It looks very neat: The issue that I noted though, are: - Gridmap Nodes are not rendered: - GPUParticlesCollisionBox3D are taken into account for the Camera distance, which may not be wanted: - the current Thumbnail's camera angle may be great for single asset with a front, but it is not ideal for a Library of Assets or for Levels. It might need to be customisable or changed to something similar to the Mesh's Advanced Import default? - We may not always want the GPUParticle3D to contribute to the Camera distance: - Thumbnails use a background colour, while for 3D Assets we might want a transparent background as seen for the mesh previewer? See `laser-gun-design1_Cube.tres` below. - it seems that the Thumbnail camera assumes that the Forward direction is +Z while in Godot the forward vector is -Z? I guess some of these issues could be solved with customisation settings that are part of another PR! We could imagine a action "Customise Preview Thumbnail" in the right-click menu where we can set the camera angle, and what to ignore.

Hi there, I've been testing out this PR on a private fork of Godot 4.7 (which also includes some other custom changes, but none that would affect either the thumbnail generation nor the asset/file browser).

I've currently got an absolutely massive project with almost all Synty Studios packs converted over into Godot (custom importer plus some generalized shaders to make the majority of the models render correctly) and the project is still working on generating all the thumbnails for it.

Overall the performance is perfectly acceptable, it's about 173K assets that need thumbnail generation so it's taken a full day already (in the background, it works faster in the foreground with Godot being the active window) and still has around 2-10 hours left to go (2 if I have the editor active, 10 if I keep it in the background). Each prefab is taking around 0.6 seconds on average in the background and around 0.2 in the foreground. I know this because I had Claude make a quick progress window to see the current status of the thumbnail generator including an ETA. And no, I won't even try to push this code back into the PR for obvious reasons.

What is an issue related to this PR though are the following two

* Cached vs render priority. 
The background thread that generates these thumbnails doesn't seem to prioritize loading in already rendered and cached thumbnails, so if a folder already has had all of its thumbnails generated, but the loading/rendering of them is at the back of the queue then you'll need to wait until everything before that is processed before an already cached thumbnail even shows up. If instead you give priority to thumbnails which are already per-rendered then these can be loaded and rendered right away whilst the remaining thumbnails still get generated afterwards in the background making everything feel more responsive.

~~* Don't load all thumbnails at once.
This might be more an adjacent issue rather than directly related to this PR, but it seems that Godot automatically tries to load in the thumbnails for Every asset in the project, not just the current folder you're in. This means that with around 110K assets already having a thumbnail (at the default 64px in size) I'm using around 3.7Gb of RAM already (without any scene actually open in the Editor). Of-course, this isn't something I would do in a real world project, but it does show some growing pains for larger projects. Having a limit on the thumbnails stored in RAM, and only loading those for the current folder could resolve this (loading in already existing thumbnails is extremely quick after all, took maybe a minute for the initial 90K to load in)~~

Slight edit, I'm pretty sure this test project is simply too big for Godot right now. It just started crashing due to the RID limit being reached since all the thumbnails are being held in RAM. This could be resolved by the second point, but at the same time that feels like just moving this issue down the line to cause problems elsewhere later on. So given the small size of the thumbnails and how comparatively little RAM it used for the 110K assets I don't see that as an issue that needs further investigation. The cached vs render priority would still be a nice to have here as that makes the thumbnails always show up as soon as they're available.

Note this test was done on a pretty powerful PC on Linux Mint. Its got an i9-13900K, 64Gb of DDR5-5600 RAM, RTX 5080 and everything is running of off one of my SSDs (a Samsung 980 EVO pro IIRC).
